newsitem.title: CHINA: China B share indices end up, foreign buying seen.
newsitem.headline: China B share indices end up, foreign buying seen.

text.p: China's B share indices ended sharply up in enlarged trading volume on Wednesday, boosted by foreign buying in shares expected to post good interim results and those that already had, brokers said.

Shenzhen's B index surged 4.20 points, or 3.15 percent, to 137.44 mainly on strong buying in Shenzhen Petrochemical (Holdings) Co Ltd. Turnover ballooned to HK$103 million from Tuesday's HK$59 million.
The issue closed at its 10 percent limit-up level of HK$2.53 as 130,288 shares changed hands.
"Shenzhen Petrochemical and other stocks with good first half expectations grabbed the market focus today," said an analyst at China Guotai Securities.
The Shanghai B index rose 1.969 points, or 2.76 percent, to 73.269 points on relatively heavy turnover of $15.267 million, compared with $6.212 million on Tuesday.
"The most important reasons (for the market's rise) were Lujiazui and Eastern Communications," said a broker at a foreign securities firm in Shanghai.
"Foreign investors bought Eastern Communications, and Lujiazui rebounded, so the market rose," he said.
Losses in Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development Co continued on Wednesday, but bargain hunting of the stock repaired damaged sentiment, helping to lift the index, brokers said.

Selling of Lujiazui had caused the broader market to fall on both Monday and Tuesday after the property developer on Friday announced a 67 percent year-on-year fall in 1997 interim net profit to 179.376 million yuan.
Lujiazui, Wednesdays' most actively traded shares, ended the day down $0.018, or 1.68 percent, to $1.052 but buying had returned after the stock touched an intraday low of $0.964, brokers said.
Volume in the share hit around 6.8 million shares.
Eastern Communications announced net profit for the first half of 1997 was 193.227 million yuan, compared with 170.792 million yuan for the same period in 1996.
Eastern Communications was the top gainer despite a morning suspension for the results announcement. The stock rose $0.130, or 9.35 percent, to $1.520.
Brokers said soaring prices of H shares, which are shares of Chinese firms listed in Hong Kong, caused some foreign institutions to turn back to Shanghai B shares in rotational buying.
"There's been some positive spillover from H shares," said an analyst at another foreign securities firm in Shanghai.
Market giant Bengang Steel Plates was the most actively traded Shenzhen B share, closing up HK$0.13 at HK$2.35, still short of its issue price of HK$2.38. Volume reached 6.9 million shares.
The Shenzhen A share index fell 9.55 points, or 2.51 percent, to 370.86 points on light turnover of 3.2 billion yuan, against Tuesday's 4.2 billion yuan.
The A index slumped 29.545 points, or 2.46 percent, to 1,170.608 points on turnover of 3.083 billion yuan, against 3.820 billion yuan on Tuesday.
The SSE30 blue chip closed down 87.703 points, or 2.44 percent, at 3,501.849 points.
